what_it_does: Spectre is a class of hardware security attacks in which a processor speculatively executes instructions ahead of time — a speed optimization — and in doing so leaks secret data through timing side channels that an attacker can observe. Many proposed hardware fixes (countermeasures) have later been shown to be incomplete, yet designers have no automated tool to catch these flaws early during chip development. AMuLeT automatically generates small targeted test programs that probe whether a proposed countermeasure correctly blocks speculative leakage across a wide range of attack scenarios. Designers run these tests against a chip model or blueprint during development — before fabrication — and receive immediate feedback on which specific attack variants the countermeasure fails to prevent.
